messages:
cara: Hey @people-ops — quick Q. My first day was 3/16, still haven't received my insurance ID card in the mail. Also noticed a benefits deduction on my first paycheck; I thought coverage started 4/1? Who should I ping?
people-ops: Hi Cara — welcome again! Can you DM your employee ID? We'll check your benefits effective date and mailing status. Also ping @luis (benefits) for carrier side.
cara: employee ID 45218 — thanks!
luis (Benefits): Thanks @cara. I looked up 45218 — your benefits effective date in the system is 2026-04-01 because you selected 1st-of-month rules. The carrier shows an ID card shipped on 3/22; tracking says "in transit." Could you confirm your mailing address in Workday? If the address is right we can push an e-card.
cara: Address is correct in Workday.
luis (Benefits): OK. Carrier can push an e-card PDF to your email in ~1 hour. If you need proof sooner for an appointment, I can DM a benefits enrollment letter you can show at the provider.
jamal (Payroll): Hi — about the deduction: the stub you saw includes a pro-rated placeholder for premiums when coverage spans pay cycles. We usually adjust on the next payroll run once enrollments finalize. Can you tell me the pay period end date on that stub? Also DM me a screenshot of the paystub (please redact SSN).
cara: Sent screenshot via DM. Thanks!
people-ops: Also — commuter stipend and relocation expense card are handled separately. Commuter starts the payroll cycle after enrollment. If you need a one-off transit reimbursement for last week, submit via Expenses > One-time reimbursement and tag 'commuter' and we'll fast-track it.
cara: Got it. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
people-ops-bot: Reminder — please complete Form W-4 in Workday to ensure correct federal withholding. Missing forms can delay payroll adjustments.
cara: Will fill out W-4 tonight.
luis (Benefits): e-card PDF sent to your email (and I dropped a copy in your DM). Please confirm receipt.
cara: I see it now — thank you everyone!
